The premise does not hold: bare Al did not outperform the carbon/Al collector at the high current. The paper says the opposite: bare Al electrodes were prone to failure at these currents[1] (Figure S3) at 4 mA/cm^2[2], while the carbon/Al collector kept a low hysteresis of 45 mV[3] at 4 mA/cm^2[4].

The paper attributes bare Al's earlier shorting to uneven plating caused by its higher nucleation overpotential, which was 19 to 12 mV[5] (bare Al versus carbon/Al).

The document gives no hysteresis value for bare Al at 4 mA/cm^2[6], so no reduction in hysteresis can be computed for bare Al against carbon/Al. The "nearly double" figure refers to earlier work with Cu electrodes, not bare Al: reported nearly double the hysteresis at[7] 4 mA/cm^2[8] (comparison in Figure S4).
